evidence: The book prints the bare value 1; we print 1 for x>0 and -1 for x<0, so the two agree on x>0 and differ on x<0. || RE-DERIVED: put x = tan(theta), theta in (-pi/2, pi/2). Then u = atan((sec-1)/tan) = atan(tan(theta/2)) = theta/2 = (1/2)atan(x), so du/dx = 1/(2(1+x^2)) on the WHOLE domain (u is odd). For v: (1 + sqrt(1+x^2))/(2 sqrt(1+x^2)) = (1 + cos theta)/2 = cos^2(theta/2), so the outer square root is |cos(theta/2)| = cos(theta/2), giving v = acos(cos(theta/2)) = |theta/2| - because acos ranges in [0, pi], acos(cos t) = |t| for t in (-pi/2, pi/2). Hence v = (1/2)|atan(x)|, which is EVEN, with dv/dx = +1/(2(1+x^2)) for x>0 but -1/(2(1+x^2)) for x<0. Therefore du/dv = +1 for x>0 and -1 for x<0. The odd-u / even-v mismatch is the entire source of the sign flip, and v has a corner at x=0 so du/dv is undefined there. || CONFIRMED NUMERICALLY (mpmath, dps=50) by differentiating the ORIGINAL stem expressions, not our simplified forms: du/dv = -1.000000 at x = -3, -1, -0.7, -0.2 and +1.000000 at x = +0.2, +0.7, +1, +3; and v(-3) = v(+3) = +0.624522886 confirms v is even while u(-3) = -u(+3) confirms u is odd. || CLASSIFICATION: the stem places no restriction on x and both expressions are defined for all x != 0, so the book's '1' holds only on x>0.
